introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2021. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae booklets may be used.
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks »).

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) Two events $A$ and $B$ are independent such that $P(A)=\dfrac15$ and $P(B)=\dfrac{3}{20}$. Find $P(A\cap B)$. *[2 marks]*

questions.corrige_markdown:
$A'$ and $B$ are also independent, and $P(A')=1-\dfrac15=\dfrac45$.

$P(A'\cap B)=P(A')\,P(B)=\dfrac45\times\dfrac3{20}=\dfrac{12}{100}=\dfrac3{25}.$

(Check: $P(A'\cap B)=P(B)-P(A\cap B)=\dfrac{15}{100}-\dfrac3{100}=\dfrac{12}{100}$.)

**$P(A'\cap B)=\dfrac{3}{25}=0.12$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(a) In a class of 200 students, 80 are boys and 120 are girls. Given that $\dfrac34$ of the boys and $\dfrac25$ of the girls offer the sciences. A student $X$ is chosen at random from the class. By drawing a tree diagram or otherwise, find the probability that $X$ offers the sciences. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$P(\text{boy})=\dfrac{80}{200}=\dfrac25$ and $P(\text{girl})=\dfrac{120}{200}=\dfrac35$.

Tree diagram: first branches Boy ($\frac25$) and Girl ($\frac35$); second branches Science and Not science: boy $\to$ Science $\frac34$, Not science $\frac14$; girl $\to$ Science $\frac25$, Not science $\frac35$.

$P(S)=\dfrac25\times\dfrac34+\dfrac35\times\dfrac25=\dfrac{3}{10}+\dfrac{6}{25}=\dfrac{15}{50}+\dfrac{12}{50}=\dfrac{27}{50}.$

(Check by counting: $60$ boys and $48$ girls offer the sciences, $\dfrac{108}{200}=\dfrac{27}{50}$.)

**$P(S)=\dfrac{27}{50}=0.54$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Find the probability that $X$ is a girl or offers the sciences. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$P(G\cup S)=P(G)+P(S)-P(G\cap S)$ with $P(G)=\dfrac35$, $P(S)=\dfrac{27}{50}$ and $P(G\cap S)=\dfrac35\times\dfrac25=\dfrac{6}{25}=\dfrac{12}{50}$.

$P(G\cup S)=\dfrac{30}{50}+\dfrac{27}{50}-\dfrac{12}{50}=\dfrac{45}{50}=\dfrac9{10}.$

(Check by counting: $120+60=180$ students, $\dfrac{180}{200}$.)

**$P(G\cup S)=\dfrac{9}{10}=0.9$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) Find the probability that $X$ is a boy given that he offers the sciences. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Conditional probability: $P(B\mid S)=\dfrac{P(B\cap S)}{P(S)}$.

$P(B\cap S)=\dfrac25\times\dfrac34=\dfrac3{10}=\dfrac{15}{50}$ and $P(S)=\dfrac{27}{50}$.

$P(B\mid S)=\dfrac{15/50}{27/50}=\dfrac{15}{27}=\dfrac59.$

(Counting: $60$ boys among $108$ science students.)

**$P(\text{boy}\mid\text{sciences})=\dfrac59\approx0.556$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)
